_comment: MORPH: THE OPPONENT-END-STEP FLIP (Morph INT-2b, 2026-11-12; morph.md step 7).
Turn 2: a face-down Blistering Firecat cast THIS turn (summoning sick), two Mountains untapped, the Forest
tapped, Berserk + Temur Battle Rage in hand, a Forest on top for turn 3. The searched line turns the Firecat
face up at the OPPONENT'S end step with the two Mountains this turn would otherwise waste: it has missed that
end step's sacrifice trigger, so on turn 3 it attacks as a 7/1 and the four lands pay Berserk ({G}: 14) and
DISCRIMINATING: flipping on turn 3 instead costs the {R}{R} turn 3 needs (two Forests left: Berserk, no
red for the Rage -> 14); flipping on turn 2 for haste (7) gets it sacrificed at turn 2's end step. Only
the end-of-turn window wins on turn 3.
BUDGETED (d3 b100). Until INT-2c this fixture was pinned to budget 0 because no searched line ever held the
face-down Firecat: with the land drop already made the main-1 menu was {flip} and no host appended a PASS
(FSLineWin's idle node / SolveWithLookahead's pass ran only on an EMPTY list), so the hold line was
unenumerable at every budget and depth (d3 b0 passed only through the root's no-win fallback plus the
executor's crossing node). TurnSolver.cpp FaceUpHoldPassMissing appends the pass while the end-step flip axis
is live. Twin: morph_eot_flip_firecat_d2_b0.json (the shallow, unbudgeted shape that also failed).
